Diagnosis:
The test that fails checks the behavior of FastDateParser when confronted with an unterminated quote pattern, specifically the format "'d'd'". According to the test, this should fail because the format pattern has an unterminated quote, but currently, it succeeds.

Examining the init() method in FastDateParser shows that the pattern used for parsing is compiled by iterating over format fields recognized by a regex matcher against the pattern string. The getStrategy(String) method decides what strategy to use for each format field. When a format field starts with a single quote ('\''), the quotes are stripped from the ends if the formatField length is greater than 2 (line 538: formatField= formatField.substring(1, formatField.length()-1);), then a new CopyQuotedStrategy is returned with the stripped content.

This approach assumes that the quotes are properly closed in the pattern string. But if the quote is unterminated, the substring operation would not correctly handle this, causing the parser to incorrectly compile the pattern without detecting the unterminated quote error.

The current init() method logic (lines 123-149) does not seem to check for unterminated quotes explicitly. It relies on the formatPattern matcher to extract each format field, but if the regex itself accepts an unterminated quote as a valid token, then the parsePattern ends up being constructed incorrectly.

This matches the bug report, which states that the format "'d'd'" (unterminated quote) is parsed as "d(\\p{IsNd}++)", effectively ignoring the unterminated quote and producing a pattern that erroneously parses the string "d3".

Therefore, the bug stems from lacking validation for unterminated quotes in the pattern string during parsing and compilation of the pattern in FastDateParser.init(). The pattern compilation incorrectly strips and handles quoted tokens without verifying they are properly closed.

No recent bug reports seem directly relevant, as they address unrelated issues.

Next, I will locate the regex pattern used to match format tokens in the pattern string that is assigned to formatPattern to confirm if this regex can cause unterminated quote acceptance.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
